opening: I run marketing for a department store group in the Emirates: stores, a website and an app. Our COO is sure app customers are worth far more than the others and wants to move most of next year's ad budget to the app. Before I agree, I want to know if that's true. The buyers also need next month's demand by category for each emirate. The table is our order history, one row per order.

I look after customer retention at a home internet provider. I want to know each month which customers are about to leave, so the team can call them with an offer. One thing: our support system counts a customer's tickets right up to the day they cancel, I think. The table I shared is our customer list with a churn flag for next month.

I'm the finance lead at a tour operator that sells city-break packages. Finance needs the bookings cleaned so they match our accounts, and then a monthly report of cancelled revenue by destination for the board. The table is our booking export. It should be ready to use as it is, the export came straight from the system.

I'm the asset manager at a city water utility. We can only replace about two percent of our water mains a year, and bursts keep surprising us. I'd like a model that tells us which pipes will burst next, so we replace those first. We'll know it works if bursts go down on the pipes we replace.
reply: We have fifteen years of burst records and a register of pipes with material, diameter, install year and street. No sensors. That's all I can tell you.

opening: We're a recruitment agency for warehouse and driving jobs. We get hundreds of applicants a week and our recruiters can only interview about forty. I want a score that ranks applicants by how likely they are to be a good placement, and then we'd only interview the top ones.
reply: We keep the application forms, who we interviewed, who we placed, and whether the placement lasted three months. I don't have anything else to add.

opening: I'm head of growth at a meal-kit subscription; we also have an office plan for companies. I need a monthly dashboard of how churn is moving in each city, and I'd like our customers split into a few groups the marketing team can talk to differently. The table I shared is our customer list.

We run a car ferry on two routes. I want to set fares per sailing automatically: predict how full each sailing will be and charge more when it will be busy. Our history should tell us how much people react to price.
reply: We have three years of sailings with fares, cars and passengers booked, and the booking dates. We've always raised fares by hand for the busy ones. I can't tell you more than that.

opening: I'm head of sales at a company selling package trips. Our sales director says British customers book much later than everyone else, so we should open British sales later. I also want to know how many trips we'll sell for each travel month next summer. I shared our bookings table.
